Tech Report: Why Liverpool have a point to prove against Man United: Andoni Iraola's side must end rotten run against 'Big Six' rivals - and Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak have to finally step up when it matters

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 01:42 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 05:02 EST, 23 November 2026.
  • Given the carousel of chaos and never-ending crises at Old Trafford, it is easy to forget there are football storylines away from the headline-generating machine of Manchester United and Mauricio Pochettino.
  • Lo and behold, there is – and Liverpool also enter Sunday’s clash against the old enemy with a point to prove.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LEWIS STEELE, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 01:42 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 05:02 EST, 23 November 2026.

Given the carousel of chaos and never-ending crises at Old Trafford, it is easy to forget there are football storylines away from the headline-generating machine of Manchester United and Mauricio Pochettino.

Lo and behold, there is – and Liverpool also enter Sunday’s clash against the old enemy with a point to prove.

One problem for Andoni Iraola is his side's frailties in the bigger games, which comes into focus this weekend with United in town – despite the desire to make an easy joke about how this is a clash against relegation fodder.

Since thrashing United 7-0 in 2023, Liverpool have beaten their friends in Manchester just once in seven meetings, including two draws and a defeat at Anfield.

To use a cliche, form seems to go out of the window for this fixture. In the last two Anfield meetings, Liverpool have been first and second in the table, United 14th and then tenth. This weekend, it is fourth against 18th, though Pochettino’s side could be bottom by kick-off.

Recent findings suggest that liverpool’s struggles in bigger games stretch further. Against the so-called 'Major Six’, the Reds have won just two of 12 games since winning the Premier League title. In a ‘mini league’ of those six sides, Liverpool are bottom in the aforementioned period.

Andoni Iraola's Liverpool side must prove on Sunday they can deliver in the biggest matches.

Manchester United did the double over Liverpool in the Premier League last season.

United did the double over Liverpool last season, Manchester City have beaten them four times in little over 12 months, Arsenal won on Merseyside a month ago.

Sources indicate that so why has this team gone from looking formidable 18 months ago to rather flappable whenever the historic major boys are in town? Casual neutrals who only tune in for the showpiece Sunday 4.30pm may joke that they have not seen Liverpool play well for a good year.

A lot of the answer to that question comes back to Arne Slot and the concerns we documented every week last season, when his side were dull and boring to watch, naked in defence and would capitulate in an instant.

Maybe players like Isak, Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola thrive more in intricate spaces rather than the gaping gaps left behind by the attack-minded bigger teams.

Another reason could be the simple fact that these sides are more likely to expose Liverpool’s vulnerabilities, such as the lack of a true defensive midfielder, the poor full backs or the frailties at defending set-pieces.

Anfield has lost its fear factor somewhat, too. Liverpool are top of the Premier League away table with 13 points from 15, but 18th in the home table with just one win in five games.

It has been revealed that city had not won in front of a crowd there since 2003, now they have done it two seasons running. Arsenal had not triumphed at the stadium for 14 years until last month.

Recent findings suggest that iraola is aware of all this and said on Friday: ‘United finished third in the table last season. You are looking at a squad with exactly the same players. They had very, very good results, especially in the second half of the season.

Liverpool bemoaned Ryan Gravenberch’s red card in their home defeat to Manchester City.

The Reds spurned a number of chances when they were beaten 1-0 by Arsenal last month.

‘Now we have just started, this is just 10 games. So, for sure, they will be a lot higher in the table (soon). We have to rate them like this and the truth is the reference we have is that they finished third.

Sources indicate that ‘We have to look at ourselves because we need the points. We need to improve our home form. It is also a major game in terms of relevance. It’s Liverpool v Manchester United, so we want to play well and we want to win.’.

Asked if he understands the importance of the fixture to fans, Iraola – who spent the weekend off taking in grassroots football and netball games following his kids – said: ‘I am very aware! This is the biggest one in English football. In this country, this is the one.’.

In Iraola’s first two bigger games, a theme threatened to emerge. Against Manchester City, Liverpool were well in the contest until Ryan Gravenberch’s red card but were toothless when it came to putting their chances away, lacking bite in attack.

The game was there to be won at 0-0, with the Anfield crowd roaring, but the Reds did not have the killer instinct to do so.

It has been revealed that against Arsenal, there were plenty of chances to equalise after the Gunners’ early goal but, again, goalkeeper David Raya could have put his feet up and had a cigar. A lot of territory but nothing to make the defence seriously sweat.

Industry observers note that in both cases, Liverpool were on the receiving end of refereeing howlers. Gravenberch’s red was not a red – the first yellow should never be a booking – and Alexander Isak had a stonewall penalty turned down. ProRef has admitted errors.

To take a cynical view, though: in the title-winning campaign, we were rarely sat talking about referees or moaning about narrow misses or unfair results. Liverpool found ways to win and had no excuses.

Liverpool need Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak to step up against the league's significant boys.

And that brings us nicely on to Sunday. It feels like the script has been written for weeks.

Indeed, after United lost 3-0 to Bournemouth and the score was read out to huge cheers at Anfield, Daily Mail Sport wrote: ‘Everyone is looking forward to United sacking Michael Carrick and then rocking up at Anfield to win 1-0 with their new manager in a few weeks.’.

It always seems to happen and it feels like United get results against rivals Liverpool and City even when they have felt close to their lowest ebb.

But Liverpool and Iraola must not allow that to happen. There can be no excuses of ‘new manager bounce’, refereeing calls or fine margins come Sunday tea time.

In a recent development, isak and Wirtz simply must step up. It feels harsh that the pair, Wirtz especially, are always in the spotlight but the £125million and £116million signings have flattered to deceive against the big boys.

Both have been spectacular at times this term but need to show up when it really matters, while £123million addition Barcola is still waiting for his first Premier League goal.

Iraola has history with United. As a player, his Athletic Club side beat Sir Alex Ferguson’s great side 5-3 over two legs in Europe.

‘I said at the time, it was one of the best wins of my career,’ he said. 'United, I remember, were champions of the Premier League, got to the Champions League final and lost to Barcelona the year before. We honestly played much better than them.’.

Iraola has remained unbeaten against United into his managerial career, winning two and drawing four of his six meetings with them.

Overall, the former Bournemouth boss has played 38 games against ‘Big Six’ teams in the league: winning ten, drawing ten, losing 18.

In a recent development, but a win is all that matters on Sunday and it is a chance for Liverpool to set the tempo ahead of a busy festive schedule. After already taking on the current top three, Iraola now contests two rivalries with a trip across the city to Everton next week.

Six of nine pre-Christmas games are at Anfield so there is a real chance to build a head of steam in the league, qualify for the next stage of Europe and get to the Carabao Cup semi-final.

Iraola would welcome those festive gifts but, for Liverpool fans, nothing will be sweeter than giving their old foes a good old walloping on Sunday.

The Brazilian winger was returning from a month-long lay-off as he came off the bench in the second half, but he lasted just 25 minutes before being forced off again, in a moment Roberto De Zerbi called “the worst thing from today.”.

His injury came hot on the heels of Sandro Tonali’s surprise absence from the matchday squad.

De Zerbi, though, will hope to welcome a number of fresh faces back into the squad before Sunday’s trip to Wearside, with a full week off between matches.

With that in mind, here is all the latest Tottenham injury news and potential return dates...

Making his first Tottenham appearance in over a month against Ipswich, Savio was unfortunate to suffer yet another injury.

He came off the bench late on, but pulled up after just 25 minutes and had to hobble off.

In a recent development, speaking at full-time, De Zerbi stated: "It is the same injury. And it is the worst thing from today.".

It remains to be seen how long he will be sidelined.

Sandro Tonali was a surprise absentee from the team to face Ipswich, with De Zerbi confirming ahead of kick-off that he is ill.

Sources indicate that the Italian confirmed that his countryman “came back (from international duty) not in the right condition. (Sandro) Tonali was sick for a couple of days.”.

Tonali was back in training on Tuesday having seemingly recovered from his illness.

Potential return date: Sunday, November 29 vs Sunderland (A).

Mathys Tel is facing up to three weeks on the sidelines with an Achilles injury.

He was on the receiving end of a crunching tackle from Jayden Bogle before the international break and left Elland Road in a protective boot before withdrawing from international duty.

Speaking before the Ipswich match, De Zerbi said of Tel: “Mathys Tel we need another two, three weeks.”.

He will be pushing to make a comeback in the north London derby.

Potential return date: Sunday, December 6 vs Arsenal (H).

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Anthropic, the frontier artificial-intelligence firm, has made history with the largest initial public offering (IPO) on record on 19 November.
  • According to recent reports, the maker of AI model Claude, Anthropic was founded in 2021 by a group who broke away from rival giant OpenAI.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Shares in the artificial intelligence firm Anthropic began trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on Thursday, in the biggest initial public offering of all time.Credit: Idrees Mohammed/AFP via Getty.

Anthropic, the frontier artificial-intelligence firm, has made history with the largest initial public offering (IPO) on record on 19 November. With a staggering valuation of around US$1.5 trillion, the firm, based in San Francisco, California, is now among the world’s most valuable companies — and it has major ambitions in science.

According to recent reports, the maker of AI model Claude, Anthropic was founded in 2021 by a group who broke away from rival giant OpenAI. Its models have proven powerful in research, and Anthropic has rolled out its own directed science effort, focusing on areas including quantum mechanics and protein design. This year alone, it has reported mathematics breakthroughs and launched its first life sciences laboratory.

It has been revealed that the IPO might also unleash a historic wave of philanthropy: all seven of Anthropic’s founders are likely to become billionaires and have pledged to donate 80% of their equity in the company to charity, including chief executive Dario Amodei. And on 18 October, the company announced that it had established the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, created to support initiatives that benefit society and stocked with an initial commitment of 5% of Anthropic’s shares.

But the firm has drawn criticism from researchers, who say its aims of curing diseases on short timescales are unrealistic and that its race towards developing ultra-powerful, ‘superintelligent’ AI models pose serious risks, including an existential threat to humanity. In its public prospectus, published ahead of the IPO, Anthropic outlines a upcoming governance structure that it states is “consistent with our commitment to AI safety and responsibility”, and adds that safety research directly shapes the firm’s “model design, training, and deployment.”.

Nature looks at four areas of science where Anthropic is making waves.

In a recent development, AI’s potential to turbocharge the discovery of upcoming medicines has been a centerpiece of Anthropic’s pitch to investors. “If today we look at things like cancer, Alzheimer’s, heart disease, mental illness — these will be relics of the past in, I think, less than a decade,” Amodei noted in a promotional video ahead of the IPO.

The company has been rapidly expanding its biomedical ambitions. This year, Anthropic opened its first ‘wet’ laboratory for life sciences research, announced partnerships with several pharmaceutical companies, and noted it was pursuing drug leads of its own. “We plan to scale this work up substantially from here,” the company said on 27 October.

Anthropic bought a one-person, AI-powered biotech: is this drug discovery’s future?

Anthropic bought a one-person, AI-powered biotech: is this drug discovery’s future?

But Amodei’s habit of promising swift, AI-fueled cures for complex diseases has rankled many researchers and entrepreneurs in the field who feel the timeline is unrealistic.

Sources indicate that over the last year, Anthropic has made a major push in the life sciences. In June, the company hired John Jumper, who shared the 2024 Chemistry Nobel Prize for his work on AlphaFold2 while at Google DeepMind in London.

Sources indicate that some of the organization’s early biological research received a mixed reception from biologists. After Anthropic reported using a swarm of AI agents to find signs of a newly introduced CRISPR-like system in viral sequence data, some researchers questioned the novelty of the finding and noted that the company had not carried out the experimental work needed to determine the system’s function.

In protein design — a field that has boomed thanks to specialist AI tools including AlphaFold — Anthropic’s work has also failed to generate much excitement. In August, Anthropic used Claude Science — an agentic system that can access other biological tools and databases — to make novel ‘binders’ against 15 protein targets.

It has been revealed that “Expectations are sky high,” says Anthony Gitter, a computational biologist at the Morgridge Institute for Research in Madison, Wisconsin. “I understand why some view their initial public results as underwhelming.”.

But Gitter is enthusiastic about Anthropic’s protein design efforts, largely because the firm was transparent about the work, from the prompts it used to the sequences that were generated. “I would strongly encourage Anthropic to continue that in their future life sciences research,” Gitter adds.

In recent months, Anthropic and other companies — notably Google DeepMind and OpenAI — have been working to establish their research credentials in large part by showing off the rapidly growing mathematical abilities of their flagship AI models.

In a recent development, on 7 September Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge and collaborator Tristan Buckmaster at New York University solved a special case of the Navier-Stokes equations, a long-standing problem in mathematical physics that describes the flow of fluids. Hours after Anthropic announced the result, OpenAI claimed a full solution of the problem, igniting a controversy.

Industry observers note that in another collaboration, Alpöge and mathematical physicist Ethan Sussman at Northwestern University in Evanston, Illinois, have been working towards establishing the mathematical foundations of the standard model of particle physics. This too is a problem on which OpenAI has made similar claims.

It has been revealed that anthropic and its competitors see the ability to write a rigorous proof of a mathematical fact as a crucial testing ground for their reasoning models. That’s in large part because the correctness of a proof is an objective measure that can be used as a ‘reward’ to further train AI systems.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Anthony Nolan | 23 Nov 2026 23:59, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 03:08.

Liverpool will travel to take on Belgian title-holders Club Brugge for a Champions League's league-phase clash at Jan Breydel Stadium on Wednesday, hoping to solidify their place in the top eight.

Andoni Iraola's side hammered old enemies Manchester United 4-0 on Sunday, and man of the match Florian Wirtz will be keen to build on his display in midweek.

Alisson Becker should continue in goal amidst reports of latest contract negotiations, shielded by a centre-back pairing of Virgil van Dijk and Jeremy Jacquet, who could be given more rest in the coming weeks with Giovanni Leoni returning to parts of team training this month.

Jeremie Frimpong was brought on as a substitute against United at the weekend, and could start at right-back on Wednesday, while Kostas Tsimikas comes in for Milos Kerkez at left-back.

Youngster Trey Nyoni has become a key part of Iraola's squad of late, and he is likely to line up alongside Alexis Mac Allister in the centre of the park, given that Ryan Gravenberch is a doubt due to a heel fracture and Dominik Szoboszlai recently recovered from a minor hamstring issue.

With Wirtz operating in the number 10 role, Victor Munoz and Bradley Barcola are the names in the frame out wide, with the latter hoping to find the back of the net after missing a number of chances against the Red Devils.

Cody Gakpo is a doubt after picking up a calf injury on international duty with the Netherlands, while 18-year-old Rio Ngumoha could begin the game on the bench for load management reasons, following his record-breaking goal and assist against Man United.

Alexander Isak has been in exceptional form this season, but he could be rotated in Brugge, leaving space for Lewis Koumas to lead the line on Wednesday.

Liverpool possible starting lineup:.

Alisson; Frimpong, Jacquet, Van Dijk, Tsimikas; Nyoni, Mac Allister; Munoz, Wirtz, Barcola; Koumas.

Tottenham have been linked to Piero Ausilio, with the former Inter Milan sporting director earmarked for a similar role at the Premier League club.

Italian outlet Tuttosport report that Spurs are closing in on a deal to bring Ausilio to north London.

It is hoped that Ausilio could be installed in time to take charge of Spurs’ transfer approach for the January transfer window.

Tottenham’s executive structure has frequently changed since 2023.

Fabio Paratici joined the club in 2021 as sporting director, but stepped down in April 2023 ahead of a 30-month ban from all football activities handed to him by FIFA after a conviction for financial malpractice.

Paratici returned to his role in October 2025 after the conclusion of his suspension, sharing duties with co-sporting director Johan Lange.

But his return did not last long, as Paratici quit Spurs in February of this year, meaning Lange stepped up to become sole sporting director.

Ausilio ended a 28-year association with Inter Milan in the summer, with the Italian giants deciding not to renew his contract as sporting director.

Initially joining the club’s youth academy in 1998, Ausilio worked his way through the ranks to become sporting director in 2014.

Midway through his first season in his role, Ausilio was named as the TMW award’s best sporting director at the start of 2015. In 2024 Ausilio was recognised as the ‘best sporting director’ in football at the Globe Soccer Awards.

Retiring from football after injury as a teenager, Ausilio holds a degree in law, having studied at the University of Milan.

Over the years Ausilio has garnered a strong reputation for his scouting and squad-building, helping to construct a team at the San Siro that has won three Serie A titles and reached the Champions League final twice in the past five seasons.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that janosch, the pen name of German author and illustrator Horst Eckert, won hearts around the world with his warm and simple sense of humor. He charmed children and adults alike with his iconic Tiger, Bear, Tiger-Duck and other animals.

Janosch created more than 150 books, which have been translated into over 30 languages.

Sources indicate that his best-selling children's book, "Oh, wie schön ist Panama," translated into English as "The Trip to Panama," was so lucrative that Janosch was able to settle down on the Canary Island of Tenerife in 1980, where he lived together with his wife Ines. The writer and illustrator died peacefully at the age of 95, his publisher Bernhard Feil declared on Wednesday.

In a recent development, janosch was born as Horst Eckert on March 11, 1931, in Hindenburg (now Zabrze, Poland) in what was then Upper Silesia. After World War II, his family had to flee to Germany.

In 1953, Janosch started studying at the Academy of Art in Munich, thinking that it would be easy to become an artist. He was however dismissed after just a few terms for "lack of talent.".

But luckily for his later readers, Janosch did not give up. He continued to work as a freelance artist, soon discovering his second great gift, namely writing.

His first children's book about a horse named Valek was published in 1960.

Although Janosch became famous primarily for his children's books, he also wrote books for adults that focused on his own childhood.

Even though he wrote cheerful books for children, Janosch hardly had any positive memories of his own childhood, as his father was an alcoholic. He was beaten not only by him but also by his mother and grandmother. Raised in a strictly Catholic environment, he was continuously threatened to be punished by God.

Later on, Janosch tried to overcome the burden of his childhood memories by turning to alcohol as well.

He always expressed a great deal of understanding for children, trying to encourage them to stand up for their rights. As a result of his childhood experiences, Janosch did not want to have children himself, and his attitude towards the Catholic Church always remained divided. "As I am a sinner and a heretic, God will let me live a long life so that I can return to the Church," he told his biographer Angela Bajorek.

Janosch's animal figures are endearing but not always well-behaved. They love all kinds of nonsense. But even if they lie to each other or put their own interests first, the true winner at the end of stories is always friendship and solidarity.

Janosch achieved his major breakthrough with "The Trip to Panama," a story about two friends, a little tiger and a bear, who set out to find their paradise in Panama. After touring around in circles, they finally end up where they started out; they realize that their journey was the destination. Janosch received the German Youth Book Prize in 1979 for the work.

Janosch's protagonists have become familiar to generations of children all over the world. They come up over and over again in the various stories carefully illustrated with water colors.

There is the honest lion Hans from the toy chest who fails to catch a nutcracker with his lies. There is Schnuddel and a ridiculous bragger Günter the Box-Frog. And then there is a tiger that collects mushrooms while looking out for his devoted friend, a bear, who always stands up for him even when the tiger temporarily leaves him because of a little pig in one of the stories.

The "Tigerente," literally "Tiger-Duck," a wooden duck on wheels with yellow-brown stripes, appears on numerous pictures by the illustrator. At times, the animal has been tossed into a corner, at times it is hanging from the ceiling, or the Box-Frog pulls it across the drawing.

His iconic figures, especially the Tiger-Duck, have served as motifs on various items, from cups to stamps to jewelry, and even on airplanes. Film adaptations and TV series based on his stories were produced in German and English.

In a recent development, guests who visited Janosch in Tenerife were impressed by his very modest lifestyle. He always said that hanging around in his hammock doing nothing was what he enjoyed most. And yet Janosch remained very active until the end of his life.

It has been revealed that from 2013 to 2019, he wrote a column for the German weekly Die Zeit, taking on the role of Mr. Wondrak, who commented on world affairs. Shortly before his 90th birthday in 2021, the complete collection of his Mr. Wondrak columns were published as a book in German.

In a recent development, like the protagonists in his stories, Janosch always tried to content himself with few things. As he wrote in one of his books: "He who needs almost nothing, has everything.".

This article was originally written in German.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Palace opened their WSL campaign with a 1-0 victory over the Toffees thanks to Lexi Lloyd-Smith’s first-half goal.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Women’s Super League strugglers Crystal Palace have been handed a three-point deduction after breaching substitution rules against Everton in September.

Palace opened their WSL campaign with a 1-0 victory over the Toffees thanks to Lexi Lloyd-Smith’s first-half goal.

But they will not be able to keep hold of their points haul from that victory, having made use of a fourth substitution window in second-half injury time, when only three are permitted per match.

That saw them introduce Kirsty Howat in place of Shannon O’Brien in the seventh of eight added minutes.

A statement from the WSL confirms Crystal Palace admitted their breach of competition rules, while an independent tribunal dubbed the move “inadvertent” and “not intended to secure an unfair advantage”. It also acknowledged Palace have taken steps to ensure the incident would not be repeated.

However, it maintained a sporting sanction would be necessary, writing: “The integrity of the competition would be damaged if a club that had breached the rules on substitution opportunities, and had won the match, were allowed to keep the points it obtained.”.

Howat did not touch the ball in her time on the pitch, which lasted less than one minute, though Everton maintained her introduction handed the Eagles an unfair advantage. The tribunal concurred, adding in their decision that Howat’s lack of influence on the match did not amount to “exceptional circumstances.”.

Rediscover your adventurous side on an exotic getaway.

The imposed three-point deduction will leave Palace on six points with 11 matches played and drop them to 11th place in the table, above only winless Charlton Athletic. Should they finish the season in that position, they would face a play-off with the WSL2’s second-place finisher for their place in the top flight.

Palace said in a club statement that they are “disappointed” by the tribunal’s decision, adding they feel they have been stripped of a “deserved victory.”.

The statement read: “Everyone at the club is obviously frustrated that such a minor infraction, given that the player was on the pitch for only 46 seconds while the ball was in play, has led to such a significant penalty – a penalty which we do not agree is reasonable or proportionate.”.

Palace do not have the option to appeal the tribunal’s decision.

By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 05:59 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 10:11 EST, 23 November 2026.

Argentina star Leandro Paredes collapsed during a live interview immediately after winning a trophy with his Boca Juniors side.

The 32-year-old was one of the focal points of a World Cup side that reached the final last summer, and went on to win the Copa Sudamericana on Saturday evening after beating Brazil's Atletico Mineiro 2-0 in Barranquilla.

But amid the thick humidity and Colombian heat, Paredes became overwhelmed moments after lifting the trophy.

After giving a brief interview, Paredes was captured closing his eyes, before falling towards the interviewer, who attempted to break his fall.

Instead, the former Paris Saint-Germain midfielder hit the ground, with attendants rushing to help him after his collapse.

Paredes had been taken off in the second-half after suffering from heat-related dizziness, with humidity at 80 per cent heading into the match, and 32-degree-temperatures.

Leandro Parades collapsed to the floor during a post-match interview after winning the Copa Sudamericana with Boca Juniors.

The interviewer attempted to break his fall as the former PSG crumpled to the turf.

'He felt dizzy towards the end of the first-half,' his manager Rodolfo Arruabarrena explained of the substitution. 'He improved a little during the break, but after 10 minutes in the second-half, you could see he was struggling.'.

Fortunately, Paredes was revived swiftly and treated in the treatment room, before re-joining his team's celebrations after claiming the South American trophy.

The star shared a brief statement on social media confirming he was fine after the interview aired.

'We're fine,' Paredes confirmed with a picture taken during treatment, before adding in a separate caption: 'Thanks to everyone for the messages, it was just a dizziness from so many turns together'.

Paredes' triumph for his club side comes months after agonising defeat to Spain in New York at the World Cup final in July.

Argentina were felled by a solitary goal from Ferran Torres to end their reign as world champions, before the match descended into petty scraps - with Paredes at the heart of the bad behaviour.

Paredes furiously shoved Spain substitute Gavi to the floor after the final whistle blew, earning himself a punchy 10-match suspension from FIFA.

He faced three assault charges, while teammate Nahuel Molina faced two, and both players were also fined $90,000 (£66,000).

Paredes himself admitted that the length of the ban had put his international future under consideration.

'It's going to be difficult for me to stay with the national team,' Paredes told the media in September. 'Because of the suspension as well, because of (Lionel Messi) Leo's decision. It's going to be difficult for everything to carry on as before.

'I haven't discussed it with the coach (Lionel Scaloni) yet, but we'll talk about it and see what decision I make.'.

Paredes' announcement came just days after Messi decided to hang up his international boots, with the talismanic Argentina superstar treated to a magnificent send-off during the early Autumn international break.

'Leo's legacy will live on forever because of what he achieved, for never giving up and for showing that dreams are hard-won, pursued and, in the end, fulfilled,' Paredes added.

Paredes updated fans after the incident to confirm he was okay before rejoining the festivities with his team-mates (Source: Instagram/Leandro Parades).

'We'd spoken in the final days of the World Cup about how the final would surely be his last match, but even so, we weren't prepared for that because of what he means to us.'.

Although unable to compete alongside him in their country's colours for one last time, Paredes joined Messi on the pitch in Buenos Aires for his final farewell, and shared an emotional tribute post to his former captain.

'THANK YOU FOR ABSOLUTELY EVERYTHING CAPTAIN,' he captioned a carousel of photos of himself and Messi.

'It was a dream to be able to have achieved everything we achieved together and to have defended this shirt and our country with you, I'm leaving and we'll miss you always.

In a recent development, 'It was a pleasure to be one of your soldiers for all these years and I will be forever! I love you buddy.'.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Senegal have been confirmed as champions of AFCON 2025 after the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) upheld their appeal, bringing an end to an ugly months-long saga.

Morocco and Senegal met in the AFCON 2025 final, but the match was beset by unprecedented controversy.

Late in regular time, Morocco were awarded a penalty, which Senegal protested by leaving the pitch.

According to recent reports, players and staff, led by head coach Pape Thiaw, alike returned to the changing rooms, and the match was paused for 14 minutes. Some Senegal players remained on the pitch and returned to the pitch only at the behest of captain Sadio Mane.

Crucially, the referee never abandoned the match, and play resumed once the entire Senegal squad had returned to the pitch.

Brahim Diaz then missed the vital penalty and Senegal went on to win in extra time, with Villarreal’s Pape Gueye scoring the decider.

According to recent reports, in March 2026, two months after the final, CAF unveiled the shock decision to reverse the result, saying Senegal had forfeited the match by leaving the pitch. The result was thus changed to a 3-0 win for Morocco.

Senegal then appealed the decision at CAS, and have now been reinstated as champions after it was confirmed their appeal was upheld.

Industry observers note that A statement from CAS read: “The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) upheld the appeal by the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) against the Confederation of African Football (CAF) and the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF, in French) concerning the final of the Africa Cup of Nations Morocco 2025 (AFCON 2025). The decision rendered by the CAF Appeal Board is set aside and the decision by the CAF Disciplinary Board is reinstated.

“Consequently, the result obtained at the end of the AFCON 2025 final is confirmed (1-0 for Senegal).”.

A decision shared in a press release on Tuesday explained: “By blowing his whistle to restart play, the referee considered that the conditions for resuming the match had been met – both teams were on the pitch again, and both expressed their willingness to resume.

“In the panel’s view, there is no doubt that the effects of the referee’s decision were limited to the pitch.”.

The panel decided that Articles 82 and 84 of the tournament rules, which formed the basis of Morocco’s appeal, were only applicable when a referee was forced to permanently call off a match. Given he allowed the match to restart and finish, those articles were no longer considered applicable.

“In conclusion, the panel considers that in resuming the match, the referee did not err in law,” the court press release continued.

“The panel acknowledged that the referee had to make a decision in an atmosphere of extreme tension. However, these circumstances do not justify describing the decision as ‘arbitrary’. On the contrary, the referee’s judgment did not appear to have been affected by factors external to the game.”.

There will be some games where Mikel Arteta has no choice but to tweak the XI, rest some tired legs and give his second-choice attackers the chance – although given the option he may wish to pick the same team every week.

The three major guns of his attack were primed and ready to come on in the next break in play when Arsenal at last broke through in this, their second Champions League league phase game of the season against some stubborn opposition from Ligue 1. Lille had sat deep against an Arsenal attack without Bukayo Saka, Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz, and the French club were past the hour when it all finally broke.

It has been revealed that that was a superb finish from Jurrien Timber who, with two touches, demonstrated that in the modern era even defenders are capable of the kind of moments of skill and composure that we once assumed were only within the capacity of the best attackers. According to recent reports, arsenal pay tribute to one of the club’s greatest custodians this evening following the news of Ken Friar’s death aged 92. Friar worked in various roles at the club across more than 70 years, and a bridge from Drayton Park to Emirates Stadium is named in his honour.

A statue at the end of the bridge is a nod to the chance meeting the 11-year-old Friar had with Arsenal manager George Allison in 1945, while playing football outside Highbury with his friends.

As Sam Dean wrote earlier today, finishing the story: “Allison was so impressed by Friar’s enthusiasm that he told him to report to his office at 9am the next day. Friar did as he was instructed and his reward was a job offer: he became a messenger at the stadium on match days. He was paid 12 and a half pence per week.”.

Friar was a long-serving member of the Arsenal board, before stepping back in 2020 and becoming life president.

After signing his new Arsenal contract last week, Mikel Arteta described May’s Champions League final defeat as “poison in his veins,” and last season’s campaign demonstrated the benefits of finishing top of the league phase.

Arsenal enjoyed home second legs all the way through to the final after winning eight from eight, and in a 50:50 draw they fell into a considerably kinder bracket.

Sometimes it can be hard to gauge the importance of these league-phase matches, but Arteta will strive for another perfect record to give Arsenal the best possible chance of going deep in the competition again.

Fixtures against Bayern Munich and Real Madrid are likely to determine whether Arsenal finish in the top two, but there is still a job to be done against Lille this evening.

Arsenal have played against 10 different French opponents in European competition but have never faced Lille, who are managed by Davide Ancelotti, son of five-time Champions League winner Carlo.

Sources indicate that lille sell their best players every summer. After finishing third in Ligue 1 last season they lost Ayyoub Bouaddi and Matias Fernandez-Pardo to Manchester City and Newcastle United for a combined £130m. They have claimed 10 points from their first five league games of the season and led Paris St-Germain 2-0 before being pegged back in stoppage time.

Leading the line for Lille is 40-year-old Olivier Giroud, who scored 105 Arsenal goals in 235 appearances between 2012 and 2018. After leaving the Emirates, Giroud went on to score against Arsenal for Chelsea in the 2019 Europa League final, but he can still expect a warm reception.

Arsenal’s home record in the Champions League has been formidable since they returned to the competition under Arteta in 2023. They have won all 11 home group-stage or league-phase matches, conceding just three goals (two of those were shipped against Kairat Almaty in a dead rubber).

Arteta’s scope for rotation has been reduced by injuries to Piero Hincapie and Martin Zubimendi, but tonight’s game should offer Eberechi Eze and Viktor Gyokeres a chance to impress, while Jurrien Timber needs minutes to build his fitness.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • German carmaker BMW reported a nearly 15% drop in third-quarter net profit on Wednesday, as competition from China shakes the global car industry.
  • Net profit for the third quarter fell to 1.45 billion euros ($1.61 billion), while sales fell nearly 6% to 30.45 billion euros, BMW stated.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

German carmaker BMW reported a nearly 15% drop in third-quarter net profit on Wednesday, as competition from China shakes the global car industry.

Net profit for the third quarter fell to 1.45 billion euros ($1.61 billion), while sales fell nearly 6% to 30.45 billion euros, BMW stated.

The main cause of the decline was BMW's poor business in China. Although the company sold more cars in the US and Europe compared to the same period last year, this could only partially offset the decline in China.

BMW's car deliveries in China, which were already at their lowest level since 2017 last year, fell 24.8% in the quarter and consequently dragged global deliveries down by 6.3.

CEO Milan Nedeljkovic said his company would "specifically intensify and accelerate structural measures.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

BMW on Tuesday also lowered its outlook for the current year, citing the faster-than-planned implementation of restructuring measures that includes 8,000 layoffs in its home market.

German carmakers have been struggling to compete with their Chinese counterparts in the electric vehicle market,  resulting in cost-cutting measures.

Volkswagen, the world's second-largest carmaker, is battling mounting competition from falling demand in its core Chinese market.

BMW, and its industry heavyweight peers, Volkswagen and Mercedes-Benz, have revealed intends to scale back production and reduce costs.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The Volkswagen Group posted its worst quarterly results in more than a decade earlier this October.

It is looking to cut about 15% of its workforce worldwide, or 100,000 jobs, by the end of the decade. BMW has declared that it will cut up to 8,000 jobs — about 5% of its workforce — by the end of 2027.

On the other hand, German auto parts supplier Schaeffler unveiled on Tuesday that it planned to cut almost 3,500 jobs and close five sites in Europe, by 2028.

According to the firm statement, three-fourths of the 3,460 job cuts and four of the five site closures will be in Germany.

German automotive supplier Bosch, the world's biggest, revealed last year that it would cut 13,000 jobs, mostly in its auto division.

Tech Report: Leading ice hockey nations, sponsors oppose Russia's return

📅 04 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (938 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) said in a statement on Wednesday that the impact of last week's Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) decision requiring it to reinstate Russia to international play had been "significantly underestimated.".
  • It added that it "maintains" its disagreement with the decision and that it remained "in dialogue with Member National Associations, organizing committees, host authorities and other key stakeholders to determine the best way forward.".
  • Shortly after Russia released its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, the IIHF barred its teams from competing in international ice hockey tournaments, citing security concerns.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) said in a statement on Wednesday that the impact of last week's Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) decision requiring it to reinstate Russia to international play had been "significantly underestimated.".

It added that it "maintains" its disagreement with the decision and that it remained "in dialogue with Member National Associations, organizing committees, host authorities and other key stakeholders to determine the best way forward.".

Shortly after Russia released its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, the IIHF barred its teams from competing in international ice hockey tournaments, citing security concerns. In last Friday's ruling, the CAS remarked that the IIHF's concerns were "not supported by sufficient evidence.".

Wednesday's statement comes after two days of talks by the IIHF Council aimed at charting a way forward following Friday's CAS decision, which appears to have caught most of the international ice hockey community off guard.

Industry observers note that two of the organizing committees the statement refers to are those of Canada, which is due to host the IIHF World Junior Championship starting next month, and Germany, which is to host the IIHF Men's World Championship next May. Both countries are strong supporters of Ukraine in its war against Russia, and both have expressed serious reservations about their upcoming tournaments in light of the CAS ruling.

On Tuesday, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney ruled out allowing Russians to compete in the World Juniors in Alberta.

"While Russia and Belarus are supporting this illegal, unjustified ​war in Ukraine, as long as that's going on, there will be none of those athletes competing for their countries in Canada," he told reporters at a press conference in Antigua, where he was attending a Commonwealth meeting.

"So, ​if you're asking specifically about the World Juniors, the Russians will not be there.".

Last weekend, Frank Lutz, chairman of the German Ice Hockey Federation (DEB) conceded in a television interview that following the CAS decision, the DEB would "also have to consider the option of handing back (hosting rights to) this championship.".

In a statement to DW on Wednesday, a German government spokesperson reiterated Berlin's position on the matter from the weekend, saying it viewed Friday's CAS ruling "very critically.".

The spokesperson also remarked  the government would "consult with the German Ice Hockey Federation in the near future regarding the potential consequences of this decision, including its impact on the 2027 Ice Hockey World Championship in Germany.".

Meanwhile, the ice hockey association of Finland, the defending men's world champions, has been spearheading an effort to boycott upcoming IIHF tournaments should the Russians be allowed to compete.

"We are at the moment working to bring as many countries as possible into a united front to tell the IIHF that none of us will play against Russia under these circumstances," Finnish Ice Hockey Association boss Heikki Hietanen said in a statement released on the organization's website on Monday.

"Our stance is that we will not play against Russia as long as the war of aggression against Ukraine continues," added Hietanen, who is also a member of the IIHF Council.

Sweden, Norway, Denmark and Czechia have since made similar statements.

"The Three Crowns will not play Russia in coming world championship tournaments," Swedish Ice Hockey Federation boss Anders Larsson stated.

This came shortly after Norway said it would not play Russia at the Men's World Championship and the Danish Ice Hockey Federation issued a similar statement on its website.

"Denmark will – based on the current situation and the information available to us today – not play against Russia at the World Championship in Germany in May 2027," it read. Denmark did not qualify for the World Juniors.

Czechia Ice Hockey Association President Alois Hadamczik confirmed on Tuesday that they too would refrain from playing Russian teams.

Latvia's federation stated it “reaffirms its longstanding and firm position" not to play against Russia or its ally Belarus.

Alexander Helwig, chairman of the Austrian Ice Hockey Association told public broadcaster ORF that “as of now, we would certainly not play against Russia.".

USA Hockey has yet to comment on the CAS ruling.

Recent findings suggest that at the same time, sponsors of IIHF tournaments are also getting cold feet. Skoda, which has been the main sponsor of the Men's World Championship for more than three decades, told the Associated Press that it would "reassess" its position if Russia takes part.

Industry observers note that "We do not support the Court of Arbitration for Sport's decision regarding the participation of Russian national teams in IIHF competitions. With Russia's aggression continuing, we believe the Russian national team's return to the world championship is incompatible with the values we have consistently upheld," the Czech carmaker said.

Skoda isn't alone either, Finnish tire manufacturer Nokian had mentioned it would end its backing if Russia took part and Swedish furniture maker AJ Products, whose logo has been seen on the boards and officials' jerseys at World Championships since 1989, said Monday it would ask for its logo not to be shown.

On Wednesday afternoon, yet another sponsor joined the list, with German workwear company Strauss saying it would "forgo all logo exposure associated with the (men's) tournament" and was considering withdrawing its sponsporship entirely.

With the IIHF Council having failed to agree on how to proceed during its meetings on Monday and Tuesday, President Franz Reindl told Germany's SID news agency on Wednesday, that it would reconvene for further talks on Thursday.

This article was originally published on November 4, 2026. It was updated on November 5, 2026 with the German government statement to DW.

Leny Yoro will be available for Manchester United’s Premier League meeting with Brentford this weekend after his one-match suspension was struck off on appeal.

The centre-back was dismissed after just eight minutes as United visited Liverpool on Sunday for a clumsy tackle on Alexander Isak.

Industry observers note that the Swede was through one-on-one with Senne Lammens and took a heavy first touch before being caught by the backtracking Yoro, just outside the box. Dominik Szoboszlai scored the opener from the resultant free-kick and United ultimately lost 4-0.

United were quick to appeal the decision, which new head coach Mauricio Pochettino and a number of his players questioned in post-match media duties.

And their appeal has been upheld, meaning Yoro will be available this weekend for the visit of Brentford to Old Trafford.

It has been revealed that A statement from the FA read: Leny Yoro’s one-match suspension has been removed following a claim of wrongful dismissal. The Manchester United player was sent off for denying an obvious goal scoring opportunity during their Premier League match against Liverpool on Sunday 22 November.”.

Speaking post-match, United captain Fernandes questioned the decision to send Yoro off, saying Isak drew the foul and was not in control of the ball anyway.

Industry observers note that “We have four officials at the game, plus another two on VAR. I understand it’s a difficult situation, but VAR can watch it again and again, with replays, slow motion, everything,” he told ESPN Brasil.

Industry observers note that “Isak puts his leg in front of Leny simply to try to win a foul. The ball is knocked forward, towards Senne’s hands. He has absolutely no control of the ball.

Industry observers note that “For me, fine, it’s a foul. But you can’t send him off because there’s no control of the ball. It’s not a situation where Isak is going one-on-one with the goalkeeper. So I think the punishment was a bit harsh on Leny.”.

In a recent development, pochettino echoed his complaints, adding: “The ball was for the goalkeeper. In that situation, if you review the VAR you can see for sure, he never had the intention to connect with Isak.

Sources indicate that “When the control was long with the striker, the ball was going to the goalkeeper, he runs and goes down. In Leny's case, it wasn't intentional. It was an unusual situation that is normal, everyone who plays football can feel it.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Sully | 24 Nov 2026 00:47, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 03:23.

Former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher has claimed Chelsea have "no chance of achieving anything" under Xabi Alonso unless they sign a physical centre-back.

Alonso has made an underwhelming start to his time at Stamford Bridge, having overseen five wins, one draw and five losses in the Premier League.

Chelsea's frailties in the defensive third have contributed to their inconsistency, having shipped 20 goals in 11 league games this term, leaving them with the fifth-worst defensive record in the top flight.

The Blues shipped four of those goals in Saturday's demoralising 4-1 defeat against Leeds United at Stamford Bridge.

Wesley Fofana and Levi Colwill started as Chelsea's centre-back pairing at the weekend, with Maxence Lacroix currently sidelined with a hamstring injury.

Speaking on Sky Sports' Monday Night Football, Carragher criticised Fofana and Colwill for their lack of physicality, telling Chelsea to address the centre-back position in the January transfer window.

"Chelsea have got a massive problem at centre-back, and if they don't change it in January, they're going to have a big problem in terms of where they feel they should be this season with the Champions League," Carragher noted.

"Colwill at Sunderland against Brobbey gave the penalty away, and the manager took him off at half-time.

"Fofana's performance against Man United, especially in the first half, was one of the worst you'll see from a centre-back this season.

"As a partnership, this will never work because they're not physical enough and there's no real leader there.

"It almost feels like you've got two novices playing, but one cost £75m, and Colwill has been talked up a lot not just at Chelsea but at international level as well.".

"Those two can't play in a back four as a two, but it reminds me of myself at Liverpool. We didn't fix it defensively and we were seen as weak, conceding from set pieces and long throws.

"It wasn't until we signed Sami Hyypia, 6ft 4in, dominant centre-back, leader, great player, that it changed for us.

"This is not going to change with what they have. Lacroix is a decent player, that's a sticking plaster until the next transfer window in January or the end of the season.

"Until they sign that dominant centre-back and leader, they've got absolutely no chance of achieving anything.".

After splashing out £52m on Lacroix in the summer, Chelsea may be somewhat reluctant to spend more money on their central defence in the January window.

However, if their defensive issues persist, they may be forced into recruiting a upcoming centre-back in a bid to add some much-needed solidity to Alonso's backline.

Recently, Chelsea have been mentioned as a potential suitor for AC Milan defender Koni De Winter, who has also been linked with Manchester United and Liverpool.

Chelsea are also stated to be interested in Lens defender Pierre Ismael Ganiou, who has drawn comparisons with former Real Madrid centre-back Raphael Varane.

Tottenham wonderkid Luca Williams-Barnett has signed a new contract, tying his long-term future to his boyhood club.

The 18-year-old was in the final two years of his existing contract, but has now agreed fresh terms.

Much has been expected of Williams-Barnett for quite some time, after impressing at both domestic and international youth levels with Spurs and England, and he has had to be patient after being given his senior debut last season in the Carabao Cup aged just 16 years old.

Two short cameos in the Premier League earlier this season led to a first senior start on Saturday for the visit of Ipswich, in which the teenager produced a star performance with a goal and assist in a 2-0 win.

Williams-Barnett became Tottenham’s youngest scorer in the Premier League since Gareth Bale in 2007 when putting Spurs ahead after just 15 minutes, before turning provider to set up Dominic Solanke shortly after half-time.

Reacting to the man-of-the-match performance, which earned the youngster a standing ovation from the home crowd, Roberto De Zerbi compared the 18-year-old to Barcelona star Lamine Yamal.

"I’m positive about that because he has great confidence. He knows all his qualities, but I think he has a very good family and it’s crucial for this type of player," De Zerbi mentioned.

"I think he’s already in a top club. He has nothing to change because he’s already at the top of the level of the club he wants to arrive. He understands because he’s smart. He’s smart to understand the behaviour.

"I think I’m positive about his behaviour, his character, because I’ve been working with him for three or four months and I know him enough to say this.".

De Zerbi said: "When I said the first 11 to the players, I said, ‘remember the first game, the debut of you, and help the kid tomorrow, because he’s one of us, and if he plays well, we have more chances to win the game.’”.

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Paulo Dybala felt personally responsible for leading Roma back to the Champions League and is relishing the opportunity to test himself against Europe's best teams.

Roma are in the Champions League for the first time since 2018-19 and have taken four points from their opening four matches.

But Gian Piero Gasperini's side, who have suffered dramatic defeats to Real Madrid and Manchester United already, face their toughest test on Wednesday, with a trip to the Parc des Princes to face European champions Paris Saint-Germain up next.

Roma have won four of their six games against French sides in major European competition (L2), but face a PSG team that have won all four of their matches so far.

PSG have also scored 20 goals in their four Champions League games this season, netting at least four each time. They are the first team to score 4+ goals in four consecutive games in the competition, while only in 2017-18 (25 in six games) and 2025-26 (21 in eight games) have they scored more in a single group stage.

But Dybala is looking forward to squaring off against Luis Enrique's side after spending his first four seasons at Roma trying to get them back into Europe's premier competition.

Industry observers note that "In my first years here, it was obviously a disappointment not to be able to bring Roma back to the Champions League. I also felt responsible," Dybala noted.

"In my first year, we came close to reaching the Europa League final, but in the years that followed we didn’t do enough to deserve it.

Industry observers note that "Last year, I saw a determined team. We highlighted that by keeping clean sheets in the last few games, because we knew qualification didn't depend on us until the final matchday.

"It was a moment of great pride for me, because I could see how happy the fans were to be back in the Champions League, just like we were.

"We want to test ourselves against the best teams in Europe, and now we can.".

Paris #ASRoma #UCL https://t.co/ASG2SWJceB.

— AS Roma (@OfficialASRoma) November 24, 2026.

PSG have faced seven different Italian opponents in European competition, but this will be their first ever meeting with Roma.

They have had at least 10 shots on target in all four of their Champions League games so far this season – no team on record (since 2003-04) has ever done so in five in a row.

Dybala and Donyell Malen have been Roma's goal threats, with the latter being directly involved in six goals in the Champions League this season (four goals, two assists). The only Roma player with more goal involvements in a single edition is Edin Dzeko (10 in 2017-18 and eight in 2018-19).

The Argentine has registered four assists in nine appearances across all competitions in 2026-27 after struggling with a calf injury.

Dybala signed a one-year contract extension with Roma during the summer, and he hopes to end his playing career in Italy.

According to recent reports, "I never imagined I'd have a career like this, let alone spend 15 years in Italy. I've lived in the south, the north, and now the centre of the country," Dybala added.

Sources indicate that "I've been here for almost half my life, and I'm very happy. Italy welcomed me with open arms. My daughter was born here, so she's Italian.

It has been revealed that "I hope to stay in Italy for the rest of my career. It would be special for me to dedicate an entire career to Serie A, as well as the year I spent in Serie B, which was very important.".

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that on November 4, 2001, London's Leicester Square became a world of witches and wizards. The occasion was the world premiere of "Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone" (released in the US and India as "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone").

"Thousands of excited fans, some dressed up in wizard hats and cloaks, gathered to catch a glimpse of arriving celebrities," the BBC reported at the time.

Daniel Radcliffe, who played Harry Potter, was just 12 years old and clearly impressed by the spectacle. The BBC quoted him as saying, "It is so cool. I have never heard my name shouted so much in an hour.".

The crowds demonstrated just how far Harry Potter fever had spread in only four years.

The first Harry Potter book was published by Britain's Bloomsbury in June 1997, with an initial print run of just 500 hardcover copies.

About 5,000 paperback copies were also released around the same time.

Recent findings suggest that today, first editions are prized collectors' items, with hardcover copies commanding high prices at auction. In mid-October, one sold for $400,000 through US auction house Heritage Auctions.

At first, the book's popularity grew largely by word of mouth among schoolchildren. Media attention followed when it won the prestigious Nestle Smarties Book Prize later that year.

With an estimated 120 million-plus copies sold worldwide, it is the best-selling book in the series and ranks among the best-selling novels of all time.

According to recent reports, for years, J.K. Rowling's public image was defined by her extraordinary rise from a single mother on welfare to a billionaire.

Sources indicate that but in recent years, debate over her views on gender and transgender identity has increasingly overshadowed that success. It's an glitch Rowling herself frequently weighs in on.

Recent findings suggest that in an essay published on her website on October 21, 2026, Rowling reiterated her opposition to what she calls the "current, dominant strain of trans activism." She argues that this movement "holds that a man who declares himself a woman is, literally, a woman, and is therefore entitled to be treated as a woman in all contexts." Rowling argues that allowing trans women into single-sex spaces poses a risk. She describes biological sex as an indisputable biological fact.

Such statements have led critics to accuse Rowling of transphobia, while others regard her stance as a defense of women's rights and safety.

The controversy has also divided her fans. Some stand by Rowling, while others try to draw a distinction between the books and their author.

Others have left Harry Potter behind altogether. One former fan is German YouTuber Coldmirror, known for her Harry Potter parodies. The media artist from the Bremen area, whose real name is Kathrin Fricke, told the Süddeutsche Zeitung newspaper: "I don't have any love left for Harry. I'm still somewhat interested, but I can no longer watch it in good conscience." She cited Rowling's campaigning against transgender people as the reason.

In a recent development, the "Harry Potter" film cast is divided as well. The three main stars — Daniel Radcliffe, Emma Watson and Rupert Grint — have publicly spoken out in support of transgender people. Meanwhile, Ralph Fiennes, who played Lord Voldemort, and Helena Bonham Carter, who portrayed Bellatrix Lestrange, have defended Rowling's right to express her views.

Despite the controversy surrounding Rowling, Warner Bros., which holds the Harry Potter film rights, is bringing the books back to the screen — this time as a series for HBO. The premiere is scheduled for December 25.

Sources indicate that the eight-episode first season is an an adaption of the first book. Even though the episode lengths haven't been announced, the scope of a TV series gives each book much more room than the original films did. That means more time to explore subplots, character development and everyday life at Hogwarts. While many fans are looking forward to a more detailed adaptation, others remain skeptical. They find it hard to imagine the familiar characters being played by anyone else.

The upcoming trio consists of Dominic McLaughlin as Harry Potter, Arabella Stanton as Hermione Granger and Alastair Stout as Ron Weasley.

J.K. Rowling is an executive producer on the show. HBO claims, however, that her views on gender identity won't be reflected in the storyline. Several people involved in the new production have publicly distanced themselves from her views. Paapa Essiedu, who has been cast as Severus Snape, signed an open letter supporting transgender people. Rowling subsequently noted she had neither the power nor the desire to have him removed from the show because of it. John Lithgow, who plays Dumbledore, and Nick Frost, who portrays Hagrid, have also spoken out against Rowling's views.

Sources indicate that meanwhile, the Harry Potter merchandising machine is still going strong. On November 4, Britain's largest Harry Potter store to date is set to open in London. According to Warner Bros., the two-story shop covers more than 1,950 square meters.

This article was originally written in German.

Liverpool have reportedly started negotiations with goalkeeper Alisson Becker over a newly introduced contract.

Alisson is just two games away from reaching an appearance milestone, having featured in 348 competitive matches since joining the Reds from Roma in the summer of 2028.

The Brazilian has been viewed as one of the world's best goalkeepers for the majority of his time at Anfield, and has helped the club win numerous honours, including two Premier League titles and the 2018-2019 Champions League.

Alisson has, unsurprisingly, remained the Reds' undisputed number one under Andoni Iraola, although there is some uncertainty about how much longer he will continue to be Liverpool's goalkeeper.

That is because his contract will expire at the end of the current campaign, which means Liverpool are currently running the risk of losing the experienced shot-stopper as a free agent.

According to Nicolo Schira, Liverpool are taking steps to address that glitch by opening talks with Alisson over a upcoming deal.

The Brazil international is said to be open to extending his stay at Anfield until the end of the 2028-29 season.

Flamengo and Juventus were mentioned to be interested in signing Alisson in the summer transfer window, but Iraola and the Liverpool hierarchy made it clear he was 'non-transferable'.

There has been some suggestion that Alisson's level has slightly dropped over the last year or so, while he also came under fire for his performances in defeats against Arsenal and Fenerbahce.

However, he showed great character to bounce back with a strong performance in the 3-1 win over Crystal Palace before the international break, a game in which he made six important stops to help Liverpool clinch all three points.

Alisson then kept his fifth clean sheet of the Premier League season in Sunday's 4-0 win over Manchester United, albeit he had little to do against the 10-man Red Devils.

The 34-year-old appears to be under minimal pressure from his current deputy, Giorgi Mamardashvili, who may have to assess his own future if it becomes clear there is no clear path to being Liverpool's number one.

With that in mind, Alisson's status as Iraola's first-choice goalkeeper is only likely to change if Liverpool delve into the transfer market for a new elite-level shot-stopper, which is not going to happen anytime soon unless the Brazilian indicates that he will leave the club.

After just eight minutes, his looks were thrown into tatters when errors from Matthijs de Ligt and Leny Yoro saw the latter sent off before Liverpool took a swift lead.

A long ball from Ronald Araujo should have been dealt with easily by De Ligt, but the Dutchman found himself in no man's land, left the ball, and Alexander Isak raced clear.

That left Yoro scrambling to try to recover the situation for his side, but Isak stepped across him and he ended up fouling the Reds forward.

Referee Sam Barrott wasted no time in pulling out the red card, and United found themselves reduced to 10 men just minutes into a vital clash.

And former United defender Neville didn't hold back when it came to his analysis as he tore into the two players at fault.

Leny Yoro is SENT OFF after eight minutes! 😱 pic.twitter.com/VKYvckvBBP.

Gary Neville torn into Manchester United duo Leny Yoro (right) and Matthijs de Ligt after the former was sent off.

Neville (pictured) questioned why the duo were playing as if they had 'never had basic training of how to play in defence'.

In a recent development, 'When I saw De Ligt's name on the team sheet I have to admit I was absolutely stunned,' he stated, speaking on Sky Sports. 'And the reason I was stunned was because of this. If you'd watched him in Como four weeks ago he was very much well off it and that is just a basic ball over the top.

'It's his problem to start with, Yoro can be further across, but De Ligt is miles away from it, then Yoro has to get further round, he reacts late, his anticipation is poor. It's so clumsy from Yoro, he makes a lot of these types of mistakes.

'You could argue Isak delays to make sure Yoro runs into him, but it's naivety.'.

Pochettino was left scrambling to think of ideas to tighten up the defence but, before he could bring Harry Maguire on, it was 2-0 through Florian Wirtz.

Maguire eventually came on but it felt like too little, too late.

'We saw him in Como and he has been out for a year,' Neville continued on De Ligt. 'It is really tough to come back. To have him out there in a game like this, he has been exposed. Yoro's positioning is poor, he has to be across, you have to cover your mate. It is bad all around from United.

'Michael Carrick will be watching and say that's what I was having to deal with.'.

Recent findings suggest that and his criticism didn't stop there. After having the chance to re-watch the incident, Neville's criticism grew even stronger.

De Ligt (left) failed to deal with a long ball as Alexander Isak (right) raced away before the foul.

Former United captain Roy Keane (pictured) added that he was 'amazed' by the errors made.

Industry observers note that 'It's as bad defending from two centre backs defending a long ball as you will see,' the former defender, who likened a return from a year out to playing after six pints of alcohol, added. 'De Ligt is well out of it - he's been out so I have some sympathy. But between them, to let the ball beat you, it's unforgivable.

'It is shocking. Whilst Man United have those types of defenders in their team, they have no chance of keeping a clean sheet.

It has been revealed that 'It's basic understanding of how to play a position. It's the fundamentals. It's like these guys have never had basic training of how to play in defence.'.

Former United captain Roy Keane chimed in too, adding at half-time: 'It doesn't matter if it's a back four or back five, you do the basics right.

According to recent reports, 'I'm amazed at this level, I know he's been out a while, but it's really poor defending. He's never getting that ball.

It has been revealed that 'If you're a defender you always expect the worst. Isak's done well and I actually don't think he's going to get the ball.

In a recent development, 'There's no way he's (Yoro) getting the ball, it's clumsy by United. Straight ball over the top and he's in substantial trouble. But there's no way he's getting that ball. I know he's quick and sharp but it's really poor defending. Players not smelling danger.'.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Millwall will play December’s match against Sheffield United under a partial stadium closure after being found guilty of “ableist and homophobic chanting” from supporters.

The FA’s regulatory commission proved breaches of FA rule E21, which regulates supporter misconduct, observed during last season’s clash with Charlton Athletic at The Den.

They were handed a two-game stadium ban as a result, though the second of those two matches is suspended.

Four blocks of the Dockers Stand will be closed for the visit of the Blades.

They have another partial stadium closure suspended until the end of next season, have been fined £70,000 and had an extended FA Action Strategy applied.

A club statement read: “Both chants are discriminatory and offensive, and the club condemns them in the strongest possible terms.

“Ableist and homophobic chanting, as well as any other form of discriminatory chanting, has no place in football or society.

“Any individual identified as engaging in such abuse will face the consequences.

“The club will continue the significant work already achieved under its dedicated anti-discrimination campaign, ‘All ’Wall’, while continuously reviewing and enhancing best practice to ensure The Den is always a welcoming environment.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that themes of relief, joy and sacrifice are commonplace in the reflections of athletes after a big win.
  • "It was everyday life, seeing people get killed around me and houses getting bombed," she told DW of her upbringing in the occupied West Bank.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that "After the referee lifted my hand to show I'm now a two-time world champion, it was a very overwhelming feeling," Mariam Bsharat mentioned. "Making history once is something, but making it twice is really something else. I felt very happy and I felt a massive relief. Only I know how many sacrifices I made and how many hardships I needed to overcome.".

Recent findings suggest that themes of relief, joy and sacrifice are commonplace in the reflections of athletes after a big win. In Mariam Bsharat's case, it's about more than just dedication to training and taking care of the body. The 17-year-old won her second under-21 World Karate Championship gold medal competing for the Palestine national team in Poland in October.

"It was everyday life, seeing people get killed around me and houses getting bombed," she told DW of her upbringing in the occupied West Bank.

"I faced challenges in transportation," Bsharat noted. "I wasn't able to go from one city to another to be able to train with other people, so that I can actually prepare for competitions. I needed to travel to other countries like Jordan or Egypt ... which was very hard for me. And, financially, the support wasn't really the support an elite athlete needed.".

Growing up in Nablus, Bsharat had a narrow path to the top. But initially, it was her own reluctance that threatened to stop a champion career before it started.

"When I was a little kid, I did not really love it," said Bsharat, who competes in the division for fighters who weigh under 66 kilograms (145 pounds).

"I started it because my family was in that sport," Bsharat remarked. "My father had a dojo, and my mother also did that sport. My siblings and my aunts and my uncles — it's a family thing. I started it because they were all doing it. In time, I started getting into it.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In a recent development, family has been a constant source of comfort and inspiration for Bsharat. Her father and uncle have acted as manager and coach respectively. While her mother and siblings moved with Mariam to Hamburg, Germany, last year, her father remained in order to take care of his business, the dojo, though he visits and tries to be with his daughter in competitions. Integration has been made easier by her mastery of the language, taught to her by her German mother.

Bsharat has mixed feelings about leaving her homeland.

"I'm thankful to be here because being in Germany opened lot of doors for me, and I think I have a brighter future here," Bsharat said. "But also being in Palestine was just my everyday life, and I loved it there. My family was around me, my friends were around me, and I just felt comfortable, which was a substantial change coming here to Germany. I think every change comes with hardships.".

According to recent reports, as well as the obvious difficulties of living in an area occupied by Israel, there are particular challenges for sportspeople living in the West Bank and the Gaza Strip, with access to facilities, travel and constant security fears among them. As such, very few people from the Palestinian territories become successful on the international sporting stage. That, Bsharat said, gives her responsibilities that are unusual and heavy for a person of any age, let alone a 17-year-old.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Sources indicate that "Being an elite athlete in Palestine is something very special because not everybody in Palestine has that opportunity. There aren't really a lot of athletes that are elite and who win international medals,” Bsharat stated.

"So all that pressure from all the country and all the people, the family, the coaches are on me because I'm representing them, raising their flag,” she remarked. "I sometimes even forget to fight for myself and actually think about myself.".

It has been revealed that that has not yet proved a barrier to Bsharat, who is is ranked first in the world in her category by the World Karate Federation (WKF). With Palestine recognized by the International Olympic Committee, Bsharat would likely have been a contender to raise that flag in Los Angeles at the 2028 Olympics. But the sport was dropped from the Games in 2024.

"The global karate community remains steadfast in our belief that the natural place for karate is within the Olympic Games, and we sincerely hope that the incongruence we suffered in Paris 2024 and LA 2028 will be corrected for Brisbane 2032, if not sooner," the WKF wrote in response to the decision in 2024. The sport was also taken off the slate for the recent Youth Games in Senegal.

Recent findings suggest that should karate return in Brisbane, Bsharat would likely be approaching her prime. In the meantime, she is looking forward to starting her journey as a senior when she turns 18. But she won't be hanging around.

"My goal is it to be a world champion at seniors, which is the hardest and the best thing you can achieve in karate," she remarked.

"But winning an Olympic medal, being called Olympic champion or just representing my country with that flag [is a thought that] is just full of happiness and pride.".

The interview was conducted by Janek Speight.
